title: Kazarma Mycenaean Bridge
visualBrief: Surviving Cyclopean corbel bridge, reconstructed as individual irregular limestone boulders, projecting horizontal tunnel courses and closing stone, battered retaining wings, small dry-joint packing stones and an uneven gravel road surface.

nativeAxes.y: up from passage threshold and lowest foundation

sourceFacts.construction: Late Bronze Age, approximately thirteenth century BCE; Cyclopean dry-stone corbel construction
sourceFacts.identity: Kazarma/Arkadiko Q254087, distinguished from the other surviving Mycenaean bridges nearby

reconstruction.basis: Authority photograph and independent 2020/2019 exterior photographs guide the central irregular opening, batter and low road edges. Major stone silhouettes are hand traced and reconstructed as chipped angular polyhedra; perspective and scale are interpreted. Individual back-face courses and buried wing extent are original reconstructions rather than scan data.

limitations: Original detailed exterior; individual boulder shapes, hidden tunnel joints and full retaining-wing extent are interpreted from photographs and published overall dimensions.
No modern safety parapet, regular Roman voussoirs, embedded source photograph or surrounding landscape is invented.

Retaining-wing road height and gully shoulders are photo-scaled relative reconstructions. Conflicting coarse DEM samples cannot resolve this narrow opening; no surveyed streambed, absolute elevation or measured public DTM is claimed.

Source-local terrain is an explicitly reconstructed dry-gully context, with the runtime tunnel opening rasterized into it. The host independently supplies real terrain; relative off-center bank contact avoids anchoring the bridge to a smoothed mid-gully sample.
